data.exact_reserve_text:
Insurance contract outstanding claims provision by year of account (YOA) as at 31 December 2017:
Analysis of claims development

named_events.loss_description: The catastrophe events of September 2017 contributed around 22% to the Syndicate's combined operating ratio.
Material losses from ... the earthquakes in Mexico

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate shows a small favourable prior-year reserve development driven by older underwriting years (a c.GBP 0.4m release relating to 2015). However the 2017 underwriting year produced significant catastrophe losses concentrated on Property (notably Caribbean losses and Mexican earthquakes) which materially increased 2017 outstanding claims. Overall prior-year movement is a modest release, while current-year catastrophe activity drove major strengthening of 2017 reserves, concentrated in Property and Financial/Professional lines.
raw_causal_phrases: The key driver of claims is the unprecedented levels of CAT activity on the Property account.
The former has contributed around 22% to the Syndicate's combined operating ratio.
material losses from the Caribbean and from the earthquakes in Mexico.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from balance sheet liabilities (claims outstanding) 2016 comparative column. No explicit note stating a gross prior-year movement was found; prior-year development was calculated from the gross claims development (cumulative) table (2015 only) and therefore relates only to 2015. The report contains narrative and net figures elsewhere (net of reinsurance) but no clear gross 'movement in prior year provision' line. All source tables are in GBP 000 and have been converted to millions. Named catastrophe impacts are described generically (Caribbean, Mexico, Sept 2017) without event-specific loss amounts.
